text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- EU objects to Russia's decision to levy border fees on travellers.
- Common law marriages becoming increasingly common as trend among couples is to get married only when a child is expected.
- Finnish rail transport safety is at average level in Nordic and European comparison, study shows.
- Employees at newspapers are the most satisfied with their jobs in Finland, research shows. @
- Finnish Post to close over 200 post offices across the country next year.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Finnish privately-owned diversified group Wihuri has bought aviation company Jetflite Oy and will acquire Euroflite Ltd Oy, raising its fleet to seven jet aircraft in total.
- Bank of Finland governor Sirkka Hamalainen is not worried by a sharp price rise in one bedroom apartments in Helsinki and there are no pressures either way on interest rates.
- State tax revenue may still rise above forecast though growth slowed in October, Ministry of Finance official says. @

- Finnish PTV4 cable channel will start operating in the Helsinki area with the signs of the coming national fourth channel Nelonen already in May-June, which is when the new channel will also start marketing advertising time.
- Growth in media advertising has been only three percent in January-October while forecasts early this year were for ten percent growth.
- Small European stock exchanges can survive in EMU, says Salomon Brothers adviser Grahan Bishop. @
- Finnish metal detector maker Metorex, created through an MBO from Outokumpu, eyes a listing on the technology-laden Nasdaq list in the U.S. but not in Helsinki.

- Valmet Automotive -- troubled Russian Autovaz' partner in assembling Euro-Samara cars -- has sufficient guarantees from its Russian partner and any change in Autovaz' structure would have no implication for it, says Valmet Automotive managing director (Optio weekly supplement). @
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- Foreign gangs of pickpockets have made a presence in Helsinki where people are used to carry their wallets in their trouser pockets.
- Many Finnish slaughterhouses no longer want to buy sheep and farmers have to seek demand abroad.
DEMARI
- Prime minister Paavo Lipponen says the EU's Dublin summit could prove historical if it brings solutions to remaining open questions on EMU. @
- Women in unionised jobs perform heavy tasks with less pay than their male counterparts, according a research by the Central organisation of Finnish trade unions, SAK.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Kesko to rent the ground floor of large Merita property in central Turku for clothing and sports retail outlets.
- Parliament wants to raise the budget for MPs' aides to nine million markka from six million, which would give each MP 5,000 markka per month for the arrangements. @
- Finn Raimo Jarvinen to donate a Finnish Christmas tree to Bethlehem. The tree is due to arrive there on Decemer 16 and be installed at the Manger square in Bethlehem.
